|------|------------------------|-----------|
| 1 | **National anthem that literally contains “Slavs”** | “Hey Slavs” (*Hej Slaveni*) – a pan‑Slavic song that became the official anthem of Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. |
| 2 | **When the anthem was adopted** |  The song was first used as the partisans’ anthem in the 1943 AVNOJ meetings, and it was formally adopted in the constitution on 25 November 1988.  For all practical purposes it served as the national anthem **from 1943** onward. |
| 3 | **Which country’s military had an “Air Defense Artillery” that was unprepared for an invasion of a country “conquered by the Pact”** | The **Yugoslav Army** fielded an Air‑Defense branch (later the Air Defense Artillery Troops).  In 1941, Yugoslavia was invaded and quickly overrun by the Axis powers, who were bound together by the **Tripartite Pact** (Germany, Italy and Japan).  The Yugoslav Air Defense units were basically unready for that rapid invasion. |
| 4 | **Putting it together** | The country whose Air Defense Artillery was unprepared for a Pact‑bound invasion is Yugoslavia.  Yugoslavia’s anthem that contains “Slavs” – “Hey Slavs” – came into force in **1943**. |

---

**Bottom line:**  
The word “Slavs” first appeared in the **official national anthem of Yugoslavia in 1943**.
